 Judgment

These two appeals are preferred by the appellant/petitioner and Insurance Company aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 17.04.2021 passed in MVC No.249/2018 by the learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT- Yadgir (for short 'the Tribunal').
2.

Though this matter is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal 3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the tribunal has committed a gross error in not considering any material evidence both oral and documentary and has awarded meager and inadequate compensation, which requires to be enhanced.
Hence, on these grounds sought for enhancement of compensation and prays to allow the appeal filed by the petitioner and dismiss the appeal filed by the respondent- Insurance Company.
C / W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2023 5

. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent- Insurance Company supports the judgment and award of the Tribunal and contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.

He further submits that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle insured by the petitioner and there is contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and same is not considered by the tribunal.

He further submits that the petitioner was taken treatment in SVS Medical College which is Government Hospital and same is produced before the Court wherein it reveals the medical expenses for a sum of Rs.64,770/- which amounts to fraud.
Hence, on these grounds prays to allow the appeal filed by the Insurance Company and dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioner.
6. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the materials.
In this case the petitioner has sought the compensation of Rs.30,00,000-00 from the respondents for the grievous injuries sustained in the accident.

sentences.text: In this regard, petitioner has relied upon the wound certificate, discharge summary, disability certificate, medical bills, X-Ray report, X-Ray film and oral evidence of the Doctor who deposed as PW.2.
Ex. P. 4 is the wound certificate wherein one grievous injury has been recorded.

Ex.
P. 5 is the disability certificate issued by PW.2 in which, he has recorded all clinical and radiological examination and effect of injuries and reported 15% permanent disability to the lower limb.
He has been cross-examined by the leamed counsel for respondent No.2, but, nothing has been elicited in order to disbelieve the report.

But,
PW-2 who has issued the disability certificate is not a treated Doctor of the injured.
Therefore, on careful consideration of the probabilities in the effect of the injury on the body of the petitioner, the 15% disability is found higher.
Therefore, I applied the probable disability to an extent of 10% to the whole body for the purpose of determination of the compensation.
The petitioner contended that he was aged about 22 years at the time of the accident.
Regarding the occupation of the petitioner there are no documents to ascertain.
I have taken consideration of the petition regarding age of the petitioner.
As such I have taken consideration of his age as 22 years.
On this basis, I proceed to determine the compensation.

However, taking consideration of his age and ability, I applied the notional income of Rs. 5000/- p.m., in the month of March 2014 that could be possible to earn by anybody even though by doing any avocation.
On these statistics, I proceed to determine the compensation on the basis notional income of the petitioner is Rs. 5000/- per month, the yearly income of the petitioner will be at Rs. 60,000/-.

Since he has sustained physical permanent disability to an extent of 10%, he has been put into loss of his future C/W MFA.CROB No. 200007 of 2023 income to an extent of (Rs.60,000*10%) =6,000/- per year.
Since he was 22 years at the time of accident multiplier 10 is applicable according to the case of Sarala Varma & Others Vie Delhi Transport Corporation and Another reported in 2009 ACJ-1298.

1,08,000/-.
Therefore, he is entitled for this amount towards loss of future income on account of permanent disability to an extent of 10%

In addition to it, he has produced medical bills at Ex. P 8,
which are revealing the medical expenses to the tune of Rs. 64,770/-.
These medical bills are not contradicted by the respondents.
As such I accepted these medical bills and hospital expenses bills to grant the medical expenses of Rs. 64,770/- to the petitioner.
Since the petitioner has sustained one grievous injury it is appropriate to grant of Rs. 15,000/- towards pain and sufferings and mental agony.
In addition to it, it is appropriate to grant of Rs. 10,000/- towards amenities and Rs.
towards food and nourishment and Rs.10,000/- towards conveyance charges
. According to the discharge summary the petitioner is found as inpatient for a period of 10 days.
So the petitioner is entitled for Rs. 170/- per day towards attendant charges as per price index and cost of living as on the date of accident.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs. 1,700/-
towards loss of payment during the course of treatment and Rs. 1,700/- towards attendant charges.
According to the Disability certificate as per Ex. P. 5 the petitioner is needed one more surgery for removal of implant.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs. 20,000/- towards surgery which is to be done.
Thus the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs. 2,41,170/-.
In order to avoid fraction, this amount is rounded off to Rs. 2,41,000/- .
